content: This medication may contain inactive ingredients, such as propylene glycol in the suspension, which can potentially cause allergic reactions or other complications. Fosamprenavir has been associated with an increase in cholesterol and triglyceride levels in the blood, a condition that can also result from HIV infection itself. Elevated levels of these substances may heighten the risk of cardiovascular issues, including heart attacks. It is essential to discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor, as well as strategies to reduce your risk of heart disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Treatment with fosamprenavir can help reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and it may be included as part of a comprehensive treatment plan. However, it is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor for guidance. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications, such as apalutamide, etravirine, and rifampin, can affect how fosamprenavir is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Additionally, fosamprenavir may influence how other medications are metabolized, which could impact their efficacy. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to unintended pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use a reliable backup method of contraception while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as viral load, T-cell counts, liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, and blood sugar levels, should be conducted to monitor your condition and response to treatment. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it has been more than four hours since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The suspension can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator, as refrigeration may improve its taste. Do not freeze the suspension, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following the guidance of your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
